candidates.original_title: Female teachers' math anxiety affects girls' math achievement
candidates.description: Teachers' math anxiety is associated with girls' endorsement of traditional gender ability beliefs
candidates.citation_sentence: Contrary to that the findings reported in Beilock et al. (2010), we did not find a relation between teachers' math anxiety and children's stereotype endorsement for children identifying with either gender (girls: r = -0.04, p = 0.59; boys: r = -0.03, p = 0.71).

candidates.original_title: Female teachers' math anxiety affects girls' math achievement
candidates.description: Female teachers' math anxiety negatively affects girls' math achievement
candidates.citation_sentence: Replicating the findings from Beilock et al. (2010), we found that teachers' math anxiety was negatively associated with children's math achievement at the end of the school year (B = -1.69, t = -2.65, p = 0.01).

candidates.original_title: Female teachers' math anxiety affects girls' math achievement
candidates.description: Female elementary school teachers' math anxiety is associated with girls' endorsement of traditional gender stereotypes about math and reading.
candidates.citation_sentence: Contrary to that the findings reported in Beilock et al. (2010), we did not find a relation between teachers' math anxiety and children's stereotype endorsement for children identifying with either gender (girls: r = -0.04, p = 0.59; boys: r = -0.03, p = 0.71).
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly describes this as a non-replication of the association reported by Beilock et al. (2010).

candidates.original_title: Female teachers' math anxiety affects girls' math achievement
candidates.description: Female elementary school teachers' math anxiety is negatively associated with girls' math achievement, but not boys' math achievement.
candidates.citation_sentence: Replicating the findings from Beilock et al. (2010), we found that teachers' math anxiety was negatively associated with children's math achievement at the end of the school year (B = -1.69, t = -2.65, p = 0.01).
candidates.notes: The replication found the negative association for both boys and girls, rather than only girls, but the authors explicitly characterize the overall finding as replicated. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
